title: Isolation of Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells
author: Devi Oktafiani
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7j5hkq6
materials: Freshly blood collected in EDTA tube
Ficoll Histopaque (Sigma- Aldrich, catalog number: 10771; Sterile PBS

steps.title: Collect and mix blood
steps.instruction: Collect 4 ml of human venous blood into an EDTA tube and mix well by gently inverting the tube several times.

steps.title: Add Ficoll to tube
steps.instruction: Pipette 5 ml of Ficoll‑Histopaque into a 15 ml centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Layer blood onto Ficoll
steps.instruction: Using a 1 ml automatic pipette, slowly layer the collected blood on top of the Ficoll‑Histopaque so that the two liquids remain as separate layers.

steps.title: Centrifuge without delay
steps.instruction: Immediately centrifuge the tube for 30 min at 100 × g, 4 °C, using a swing‑out bucket. A fixed‑angle rotor may be used but requires extra caution when later separating the interphase.

steps.title: Aspirate PBMC layer
steps.instruction: Aspirate the whitish buffy coat (≈1 ml PBMCs) from the interphase between the Ficoll and the medium without delay; avoid letting the tube stand >10 min to prevent the cells from settling.

steps.title: Wash cells twice
steps.instruction: Resuspend the aspirated cells in 10 ml sterile PBS and centrifuge at 100 × g for 10 min. Discard the supernatant, then repeat the wash a second time with another 10 ml PBS.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 10 ml PBS, centrifuge 100 × g, 10 min.
Repeat with a second 10 ml PBS wash.

steps.title: Remove residual PBS
steps.instruction: After the second wash, carefully discard all remaining PBS supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend and transfer cells
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml PBS to the cell pellet, gently resuspend, and transfer the suspension into a new 1.5 ml tube.
